gitCommit.subject: Grant Premium from App Store subscriptions
gitCommit.body:
Grant Premium from App Store subscriptions

Half of the fix for the Guideline 3.1.1 rejection: the server has to recognise
an App Store subscriber before the app can sell to one.

- ApplePremiumSubscription is its own model, not columns on users. Stripe
  billing already lives entirely in Pay::Customer/Pay::Subscription; users
  stays identity and auth.
- SubscriptionAccess#active_paid_subscription? ORs in the entitlement. That one
  change is what makes an Apple subscriber clear every existing gate without
  touching any of them.
- User#billing_interval/amount/currency delegate to whichever source is live,
  and the five call sites now ask the user rather than a processor. Both
  records answer the same three methods, so no view branches per processor —
  the drift that produced the advertised-vs-charged mismatch in b984919.
- RevenueCat webhook: shared-secret auth that fails closed when the env var is
  missing, idempotent upsert, own IP throttle since the general API throttle
  keys on a Bearer token this endpoint does not carry. Every recognised
  condition returns 200; RevenueCat retries non-2xx forever, so a permanent
  condition must be acknowledged, not retried.
- Sandbox events are honoured deliberately: App Review tests with a Sandbox
  account, and rejecting them would fail Guideline 2.1 all over again.
- Stripe checkout and portal now refuse Apple-billed users instead of creating
  a Stripe customer for them. The server cannot cancel an App Store plan, so a
  double charge would have to be untangled by hand.

Fixes two bugs found on the way: GET /api/v1/subscription used a stricter
lookup than the user payload, so an Apple subscriber would read "active" in one
place and null in the other; and the web /subscription page keyed its
membership card on a Pay row, so it offered to sell Premium to someone already
paying for it.
